issues.explanation: The change ships no Pest/PHPUnit tests at all, although the project requires a test for every feature and unauthorized/tamper tests for each Livewire action, so the definition of done is not met.

Creating the entity and its owner membership is a domain write performed inline in the component instead of an `app/Actions/*` class authorizing inside the action, which is the project's stated pattern.
The custom `current_entity` middleware is only aliased; it is not registered with `Livewire::addPersistentMiddleware`, so it silently stops applying on `/livewire/update` requests to the dashboard.
`entity.pick` authorizes by comparing `membershipFor()` to null instead of using the existing `EntityPolicy::view`/`$this->authorize`, bypassing the project's policy-only authorization rule.
The Blade view reads `session('current_entity_id')` directly, but the task says only the HTTP layer (the middleware/tenant context) reads that session key.

The server-only `Entity $entity` property is not `#[Locked]` and its authorization runs only in `mount`, so nothing re-checks authorization if the property is tampered with on a later Livewire request.

The `/home` closure duplicates the middleware's 0/1/>1 dispatch logic, and `$membership->entity ?? Entity::findOrFail(...)` turns a soft-deleted entity into a 404 instead of dispatching like the middleware.
`auth()->user()->memberships()->count()` runs an extra query on every page render; a shared view variable or already-loaded relation would avoid it.
Entity creation is an unauthenticated-by-rate writes-heavy action that is not rate-limited, although the Livewire policy asks for throttling on sensitive actions.

review.summary: The change adds the entities/entity_memberships model, policies, tenant-session middleware, onboarding, switcher, dashboard, routes, lang keys and docs, and covers the task's main requirements coherently. It fails the project's test-first rule entirely, and it puts a domain write in the Livewire component, bypasses policies for the picker and does not persist the tenant middleware for Livewire updates, so it needs changes before merging.
